focal_entities.audience: the user approving the UX at the ux sign-off, and whoever makes the README and the architecture from it

goal_orientation.purpose: approving what the tool gives them and how they use it, and building the README and the tool to it

goal_orientation.serves: AC1: Run plainly, with no instruction to move, on the trial folder, the tool prints a list giving each file of the six types (Images, Documents, Archives, Audio, Video, Installers, told apart by extension) with the type folder it would move to, each file of no type as not moved, and the same-name file as not moved because of the same name; afterwards every file and folder is where it was. The trial folder is a folder holding files of all six types, a file with no extension, a file with an extension of none of the six types, a folder, a hidden file such as `.DS_Store`, and a file whose name is already taken in the type folder it would move to.

AC2: Run told to move, on the trial folder, the tool moves each file the list gives as moving into its type folder inside the trial folder, and leaves the files of no type, the folder, the hidden file and the same-name file where they were; afterwards the trial folder holds the same files, by name and content, as before, none lost, renamed or overwritten, and nothing outside it is changed.
AC3: Given no folder, the tool organizes `~/Downloads`; given a folder, it organizes that folder and leaves `~/Downloads` as it was.

constraints.decision: Command name: The command is named sort-downloads.
How to tell it to move: The user tells the tool to move by adding the option --move, as in sort-downloads --move; without it nothing moves.
How to give a folder: The user gives a folder by writing it after the command, as in sort-downloads ~/Desktop or sort-downloads --move ~/Desktop; with none written, ~/Downloads is organized.
